♻ ☆ Quantum Channel Testing in Average-Case Distance
Gregory Rosenthal, Hugo Aaronson, Sathyawageeswar Subramanian, Animesh Datta, Tom Gur
We study the complexity of testing properties of quantum channels. First, we show that testing identity to any channel $\mathcal N: \mathbb C^{d_{\mathrm{in}} \times d_{\mathrm{in}}} \to \mathbb C^{d_{\mathrm{out}} \times d_{\mathrm{out}}}$ in diamond norm distance requires $Ω(\sqrt{d_{\mathrm{in}}} / \varepsilon)$ queries, even in the strongest algorithmic model that admits ancillae, coherence, and adaptivity. This is due to the worst-case nature of the distance induced by the diamond norm. Motivated by this limitation and other theoretical and practical applications, we introduce an average-case analogue of the diamond norm, which we call the average-case imitation diamond (ACID) norm. In the weakest algorithmic model without ancillae, coherence, or adaptivity, we prove that testing identity to certain types of channels in ACID distance can be done with complexity independent of the dimensions of the channel, while for other types of channels the complexity depends on both the input and output dimensions. Building on previous work, we also show that identity to any fixed channel can be tested with $\tilde O(d_{\mathrm{in}} d_{\mathrm{out}}^{3/2} / \varepsilon^2)$ queries in ACID distance and $\tilde O(d_{\mathrm{in}}^2 d_{\mathrm{out}}^{3/2} / \varepsilon^2)$ queries in diamond distance in this model. Finally, we prove tight bounds on the complexity of channel tomography in ACID distance.
♻ ☆ Express Language Modeling
Albert Gong, Annabelle Michael Carrell, Raaz Dwivedi, Lester Mackey
We introduce a new tool, Express, for converting a non-causal attention approximation into a causal approximation with matching approximation guarantees. When combined with the state-of-the-art Thinformer approximation, Express improves upon the best known causal attention guarantees, delivering $\log^{3/2}(n)/s$ approximation error with only $O(s)$ memory and $O(s^2 \log^2(n))$ compression overhead for a sequence of length $n$. We pair these developments with an efficient I/O-aware Triton implementation, demonstrate substantial speedups over FlashAttention 2, and use Express to overcome four resource bottlenecks in the language modeling pipeline: long-context prefill, KV cache compression, long-form memory-constrained decoding, and long-form compute-constrained decoding.
♻ ☆ Polynomial-time computation of $\ell_p$-contraction fixed points for even $p$
Constantinos Daskalakis, Gabriele Farina, Brian Hu Zhang
We give a $\text{poly}(d, p, \log(1/ε))$-time algorithm that computes an $ε$-approximate fixed point of any $\ell_p$-nonexpansive map $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X}$, where $\mathcal{X} \subset \mathbb R^d$ is a convex compact set and $p$ is an even integer. This is the first algorithm with $\text{poly}(d, \log(1/ε))$ runtime for any fixed $p \ne 2$. Our techniques are based on a computationally efficient version of Sion's theorem for non-compact minmax problems, and extend to more general total search problems that admit low-degree polynomial potentials.
♻ ☆ On the Parameterized Complexity of Grundy Domination and Zero Forcing Problems
Robert Scheffler
We consider two different problem families that deal with domination in graphs. On the one hand, we focus on dominating sequences. In such a sequence, every vertex dominates some vertex of the graph that was not dominated by any earlier vertex in the sequence. The problem of finding the longest dominating sequence is known as $\mathsf{Grundy~Domination}$. Depending on whether the closed or the open neighborhoods are used for domination, there are three other versions of this problem: $\mathsf{Grundy~Total~Domination}$, $\mathsf{L\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$, and $\mathsf{Z\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$. We show that all four problem variants are $\mathsf{W[1]}$-complete when parameterized by the solution size. On the other hand, we consider the family of zero forcing problems which form the parametric duals of the Grundy domination problems. In these problems, one looks for the smallest set of vertices initially colored blue such that certain color change rules are able to color all other vertices blue. It has been shown that the dual of $\mathsf{Z\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$, known as $\mathsf{Zero~Forcing~Set}$, is in $\mathsf{FPT}$ when parameterized by the treewidth or the solution size. We extend the treewidth result to the other three variants of zero forcing and their respective Grundy domination problems. Our algorithm also implies an $\mathsf{FPT}$ algorithm for $\mathsf{Grundy~Domination}$ when parameterized by the number of vertices that are not in the dominating sequence. In contrast, we show that $\mathsf{L\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$ is $\mathsf{W[1]}$-hard for that parameter.
comment: version published in the Journal of Computer and System Sciences
♻ ☆ Online Fair Division Meets Reordering Buffers NeurIPS 2026
Georgios Amanatidis, Giulio Giaconi, Evangelos Markakis, Nicos Protopapas
We study the online fair division of indivisible mixed manna among agents with additive valuation functions. Under the standard online model, at each time step an indivisible item arrives; each agent may assign it a positive, negative, or zero value, and it must be irrevocably allocated, before the arrival of the next item. At the same time, we also wish to maintain some fairness guarantee, and in this work we focus on envy-freeness (EF) and one of its most prominent relaxations, envy-freeness up to one item (EF1). Given the strong negative and the scarce positive results for this problem without additional assumptions, we augment our algorithms with buffers that can store and rearrange a limited number of items. This setting interpolates naturally between the fully online case (no buffer) and the fully offline case (a buffer large enough to hold all items). We show that algorithms equipped with reasonably sized buffers can achieve strong guarantees for personalized $k$-value instances, i.e., instances in which each agent assigns at most $k$ distinct values to items. In particular, we construct allocations that are EF1 at every time step and EF at most time steps, using a buffer of size linear in $k$ and in the number of agents. Our approach relies on novel combinatorial arguments and on constructing a sequence of envy-free matchings that allocates most items. Finally, we extend our results to general additive valuation functions, with a dependence on the largest per-agent ratio between two values of the same sign, and we also identify limitations of our approach via impossibility results on the use of buffers with smaller size.
comment: A conference version of this work appears in the Proceedings of the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
♻ ☆ Random Abstract Cell Complexes
Josef Hoppe, Michael T. Schaub
In machine learning and signal processing, methods based on (abstract) cell complexes (CCs) are being applied successfully in different applications. However, there is currently a lack of random models, which are necessary for a thorough evaluation of these methods, both by generating synthetic data and as null models to compare results to. We fill this gap by defining a random model for abstract cell complexes based on independent inclusion probabilities, similar to the Erdős-Rényi model for graphs. We also discuss how modifications to bias the model to incorporate more structure can be implemented. The model can also be used to lift a graph (or other cell complex) to a cell complex of arbitrary dimension. The main challenge in this is that the number of cycles (possible 2-cells) on graphs is exponential, and the same is true in higher dimensions. We overcome this complexity with an approximate sampling algorithm limited to 2-cells (polygons) that is based on a recent advance in sampling cycles on a graph. Using this algorithm, we analyze the properties of random 2-dimensional CCs and showcase its usage as a performance baseline for both topological signal processing and topological deep learning. The algorithm is available in the package py-raccoon on the Python Package Index.
comment: 9 pages, 7 figures (plus appendix). For evaluation code, see https://github.com/josefhoppe/random-abstract-cell-complexes
♻ ☆ Adaptive Power Iteration Method for Differentially Private PCA
Ta Duy Nguyen, Alina Ene, Huy Le Nguyen
We study $\left(ε,δ\right)$-differentially private algorithms for the problem of approximately computing the top singular vector of a matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$ where each row of $A$ is a data point in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$. Following Dwork-Talwar-Thakurta-Zhang (STOC 2014), we consider the privacy model where neighboring inputs differ by one single row. We give a novel algorithm that achieves beyond-worst-case guarantees for input matrices with low coherence, which is a structural property of matrices in many applications, including but not limited to i.i.d. data. Our algorithm contributes to the extensive literature on private power iteration methods, where we introduce a new filtering technique which adapts to this coherence parameter. Our work departs from and complements the work by Hardt-Roth (STOC 2013) which achieves beyond-worst-case guarantees for the more restrictive privacy model where neighboring inputs differ in one single entry by at most 1.
♻ ☆ Online Nonconvex Decision Making with Approximate Oracles
Rui Chen, Oktay Gunluk, Andrea Lodi, Guanyi Wang
We study online decision making with possibly nonconvex (for example, combinatorial or integer) local feasible sets and convex long-term constraints. At each period, a decision maker selects a local action to maximize cumulative reward while ensuring that the sequence of actions satisfies the global constraints in the long term. It is known that $O(\sqrt{T})$ long-term constraint violation and $O(\sqrt{T})$ reward regret are achievable if given access to a local optimization oracle that exactly solves optimization problems over each local feasible set. Instead of requiring exact optimization over each local feasible set, we assume access to an approximate local optimization oracle that permits optimization errors quantified by two parameters $(δ_+,δ_\times)$. We develop an approximate online dual mirror descent algorithm and show that its guarantees depend on a feasibility slack parameter $\underline d$, which measures the compatibility between local feasible sets and the long-term constraint. Under the standard random permutation model, when $δ_+=O(1)$, $δ_\times<\underline d$ and $\underline d-δ_\times=Ω(1)$, the algorithm achieves $O(\sqrt T)$ long-term constraint violation and reward regret up to $O\bigl(\sqrt T+δ_\times T\bigr)+δ_+ T$. We also show a matching limitation: when $δ_+=0$ and $δ_\times>\underline d$, no online algorithm relying on such approximate oracle outputs can guarantee sublinear long-term constraint violation in general.
♻ ☆ Constrained and Composite Sampling via Proximal Sampler
Thanh Dang, Jiaming Liang
We study two log-concave sampling problems: constrained sampling and composite sampling. First, we consider sampling from a distribution proportional to $e^{-f}$ on a convex set $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, where $f$ is convex. Using an epigraph lifting, we reduce this problem to uniform sampling up to a one-dimensional exponential tilt over a convex set in $\mathbb R^{d+1}$. We then apply the proximal sampler to the lifted distribution. We develop an unbiased implementation of its restricted Gaussian oracle by using the cutting-plane method and rejection sampling, requiring only a separation oracle for $K$ and evaluation and subgradient oracles for $f$, without relying on projections or barrier functions. Second, we study composite sampling from $e^{-f-h}$, where $f$ and $h$ are closed and convex. This structure arises naturally in Bayesian inference, where $f$ represents data fidelity and $h$ encodes prior information. By applying an epigraph lifting to $h$, we reduce composite sampling to constrained sampling in $\mathbb R^{d+1}$, allowing us to build on the approach developed in the first part. This leads to a double lifting formulation in $\mathbb R^{d+2}$, for which we implement the proximal sampler using different combinations of subgradient and proximal oracles for $f$ and $h$. We establish mixing time bounds in Rényi and $χ^2$ divergences for both problems. Finally, we revisit the convergence analysis of the proximal sampler from a variational perspective. Starting from variational formulations of its two half-steps as optimization problems over probability measures, we use a dynamic formulation of entropy-regularized optimal transport to recast them as optimal control problems. This allows us to derive their governing PDEs directly through the lens of optimization, without first analyzing particle-level SDEs.
♻ ☆ Log-Averaged Mirror Prox for Fast, Large-Scale Optimal Transport in Linear Space

We propose Log-Averaged Mirror Prox (LAMP), a linear-space primal-dual method for large-scale optimal transport. LAMP implements primal mirror prox updates by tracking an averaged dual sequence, reducing storage complexity from $\mathcal{O}(nm)$ to $\mathcal{O}(n+m)$ while preserving dense, GPU-friendly reductions. Consequently, LAMP preserves the last-iterate $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\|C\|_\infty nm\varepsilon^{-1})$ arithmetic complexity of conservatively parameterized primal-dual mirror prox. We further analyze LAMP as a direct optimal transport solver in a more performant parameter regime, providing a last-iterate sub-optimality certificate dependent on infeasibility and an explicit $\mathcal O(\|C\|_\infty\log (m)/t)$ term. Moreover, we give a computable sufficient condition for ergodic convergence. Numerical experiments with an optimized CUDA implementation show that LAMP outperforms first-order baselines in several high-accuracy (entropic) optimal transport problems. LAMP is further shown to scale up to problems with $n=m=2^{18}$ marginal supports, which were previously beyond the reach of primal-dual first-order methods.

Graphics 6
☆ DIRT: Depth-completed Image-based Rendering using Two-band Blending for Live Novel-view Synthesis
Mathias Harrer, Laura Fink, Noah Lewis, Paul Himmler, Tim Weyrich
State-of-the-art novel-view synthesis (NVS) methods commonly require per-scene optimization before rendering, limiting their applicability in live settings. Live or ad-hoc NVS, however, demands low-latency rendering during capture and strong generalization to new scenes. Some previous work tried to address this task by adapting training- and optimization-based methods, trading quality for low latency. We introduce a live NVS approach following traditional image-based rendering that operates on a posed set of depth sensor observations and images. Our method leverages explicit, sparse point-based geometry obtained from active sensors, resulting in a sparsely filled depth buffer that is completed in the (novel) target view's screen-space. Using this proxy, a posed set of images is projected into the target frame before fusing the resulting observations through a frequency-aware two-band blending strategy. The pipeline is entirely non-neural and optimization-free, requiring no training data or scene-specific optimization. As a result, our approach reduces the delay between capture and novel-view rendering and does not rely on favorable network generalization. We validate the method's applicability to heterogeneous sensor setups - including handheld RGB-D cameras, automotive LiDAR, and thermal cameras - as well as challenging scenarios, such as low light captures. Our experiments demonstrate that the approach outperforms prior methods in live reconstruction scenarios, while maintaining competitive performance in conventional NVS benchmarks.
comment: 8 pages main paper + 2 pages of references + 9 pages supplementary material
☆ TetraCoder: Adaptive Tetrahedral Encoding for Neural Fields
Daniele Della Pietra, Antonella Rech, Nicola Conci, Nicola Garau
Implicit and explicit representations of geometry are central in computer graphics applications and come with their pros and cons. With surface sampling being faster on explicit representations and spatial queries being faster on implicit representations, finding efficient conversions between them is a highly desirable property. We present TetraCoder, a single resolution hash-free adaptive tetrahedral encoding that links an explicit tetrahedral spatial encoder with an underlying implicit signed distance field (SDF). The resulting hybrid implicit-explicit space is continuous piecewise affine (CPWA) by design, allowing to obtain an exact correspondence between the implicit SDF and the explicit analytic mesh. TetraCoder's design comes with additional perks, in particular: (a) it scales better than multi-resolution encoding methods due to its single resolution optimizable grid, (b) unlike hash-based methods, it is not affected by collisions, (c) it enables fast tetrahedral ray-tracing, geometry and appearance editing, directly through its adaptive tetrahedral scaffold. We demonstrate the versatility of TetraCoder by showing an improvement over state-of-the-art methods on multiple tasks: 2D/3D fitting from images and point clouds, 3D novel view synthesis, 3D reconstruction, and geometry/appearance editing.
comment: 8 pages, 4 figures
☆ Pose-based Neural Clothing for Animated Characters SIGGRAPH
Julian N. Heidenreich, Vinicius C. Azevedo, Jakob Buhmann, Lento Manickathan, Arnold Moon, Paul Kanyuk, Amit H. Bermano, Jingwei Tang
Traditional garment simulation for animated characters is a time-consuming bottleneck for artists due to slow simulations and tedious parameter tunings.Recent data-driven methods offer a powerful alternative, capable of learning from a dataset of simulated data to generate high-quality deformations. A lightweight network design allows data-driven systems to achieve a real-time inference speed. This significantly improves the artist workflow, as they can interactively pose a character and see high-quality folds and wrinkles at animation time, thereby allowing to make creative decisions ahead of time. However, existing neural clothing methods have presented appealing results on datasets based on realistic human models (\eg SMPL), but when trained on animated character datasets, they struggle to generalize to unseen poses. In this paper, we aim at designing neural networks and training strategies to generalize better to unseen poses in real-time to enable the interactive posing applications. We focus on a production-oriented setting where the model is trained for a single garment in a quasi-static setup. Technically, we leverage a smooth, expressive latent space by first training a Variational Auto-Encoder (VAE). We then progressively train the VAE encoder to transition from reconstruction to pose-driven prediction. To guide this prediction, we condition the network on both low-dimensional pose parameters and character body surface displacements. Finally, we introduce a novel local gradient histogram loss that mitigates the over-smoothing effect of reconstruction losses. Extensive evaluations on production-level assets and public datasets demonstrate that our method produces sharp, realistic wrinkles, smooth large-scale drape, and temporal coherence in real-time, offering a robust and easily integrable solution for interactive posing workflows.
comment: 19 pages, 18 figures, 5 tables. Includes appendix. Accepted to the ACM SIGGRAPH / Eurographics Symposium on Computer Animation (SCA 2026); to appear in Computer Graphics Forum
☆ Creative Product Design under Brand Image Constraints
Takeshi Onishi, Hiroya Makino, Takahiro Yamaguchi, Hiroyuki Sakai
Industrial design requires creative visual exploration while satisfying constraints that are often product-specific and implicit. Existing text-to-image (T2I) approaches can generate creative designs through concept blending or multi-agent self-enhancement, but they provide limited mechanisms for ensuring that generated designs remain consistent with such constraints. We focus on brand image as a representative design constraint and propose a framework for brand-aware redesign generation. Given a product name, the framework constructs a brand image survey report that summarizes product and market information, derives a creative direction from the report, and integrates this direction into a self-enhancement loop in which generated images are critiqued and prompts are revised. We evaluate the framework on 50 redesign tasks across five product categories, comparing it with Naive T2I, IP-Adapter/IT-Blender, and unconstrained self-enhancement under the same T2I backbone. By a VLM-as-Judge protocol to measure creativity and brand identifiability, the proposed framework achieves a more favorable trade-off between the two objectives, with particularly clear gains in highly constrained categories such as automotive and motorcycle, where the plausible design space is relatively limited compared with that of other product categories. These results suggest that dynamically eliciting and textualizing brand image can guide creative product design generation under brand image constraints.
♻ ☆ Assessing the CAD Capabilities of General-Purpose AI Models: A Case Study of GPT-6 Astra
Qiang Zou, Jiajun Shen, Zhijie Yang, Yuhao Wang, Shitianyi Leng, Dongshuo Yin
Recent advances in general-purpose AI models and agentic systems have enabled them to perform some CAD tasks. A systematic assessment is now needed to establish what these systems can accomplish and how well their outputs meet engineering requirements. This paper presents an empirical study of GPT-6 Astra, a SOTA general-purpose AI model, across four basic CAD tasks: model understanding, generation, editing, and evaluation. We design test cases spanning different levels of complexity and engineering requirements. The results show that GPT-6 Astra can support multiple stages of CAD workflows, with successful outcomes in cases involving nontrivial geometric complexity. This suggests that general-purpose AI is beginning to offer practical value in almost all steps in CAD workflow. However, gaps remain between generating visually plausible geometry and producing valid, functional, and editable CAD models. Recurring errors in freeform geometry, parameter dependencies, and mating relationships between parts limit engineering usefulness. Agentic iterative refinement can improve results but does not consistently resolve critical errors; long completion times further constrain practical use.
comment: The paper contains 180 page long full report of CAD Capabilities of General-Purpose AI Models, and its 12 pages of summary. The project page is at: https://qiang-zou.github.io/projects/icad-eval-report/
♻ ☆ Human-Data Interaction, Exploration, and Visualization Systems in the AI Era: Challenges and Opportunities
Jean-Daniel Fekete, Yifan Hu, Dominik Moritz, Arnab Nandi, Senjuti Basu Roy, Eugene Wu, Nikos Bikakis, George Papastefanatos, Panos K. Chrysanthis, Guoliang Li, Lingyun Yu
The rapid advancement of AI is transforming human-centered systems, with profound implications for human-AI interaction, human-data interaction, and visual analytics. In the AI era, data analysis increasingly involves large-scale, heterogeneous, and multimodal data that is predominantly unstructured, as well as foundation models such as LLMs and VLMs, which introduce additional uncertainty into analytical processes. These shifts expose persistent challenges for human-data interactive systems, including perceptually misaligned latency, scalability constraints, limitations of existing interaction and exploration paradigms, and growing uncertainty regarding the reliability and interpretability of AI-generated insights. Responding to these challenges requires moving beyond conventional efficiency and scalability metrics, redefining the roles of humans and machines in analytical workflows, and incorporating cognitive, perceptual, and design principles into every level of the human-data interaction stack. This paper investigates the challenges introduced by recent advances in AI and examines how these developments are reshaping the ways users engage with data, while outlining limitations and open research directions for building human-centered AI systems for interactive data analysis in the AI era.
